title: The repository's own static release-checks script fails at the release commit, and no CI workflow runs it
component: supply chain and release tooling (nonos-ci, tools/nix)
description: The repository carries a static-checks script meant to prove, among other things, that no release build path can select the development capsule set, the development catalogue, or an image capability ceiling that disagrees with the shipped capsules. Run directly against the audited release commit, the script exits with failure: several of its checks are written against source text that no longer matches the current code (the code itself, read separately, still appears to enforce what the stale check text describes), and one check, the image-ceiling self-test, fails two of its five cases outright. Separately, no workflow in the repository's CI configuration runs this script; the workflow it names in its own header does not exist, and the verification workflow that does run does not include it in what gates a release.
impact: Because this gate is not wired into CI and is not green even run by hand, it cannot currently catch a real regression in the properties it claims to check, even though those underlying properties were not shown to be broken by this check. This is a gap in the audit trail the project's own tooling is meant to provide, not a demonstrated hole in the release process itself.
scenario: A maintainer or reviewer runs the repository's own static-checks script against the tagged release commit, expecting it to pass as part of confirming the release is sound.

The script fails with more than a dozen errors, most from stale pattern text rather than a real defect in the code it is checking, obscuring the one check that does show a real mismatch (the image-ceiling self-test).

steps: Ran the script directly against a checkout of the audited commit: exit code 1, final line reporting overall failure, with errors naming checks for the development-capsule-set path, the development-catalogue path, the image-capability-ceiling self-test, a proof-features check, a firmware-pin check, and others.

For the two text-pattern checks examined in detail, the current source code was read separately and still appears to implement the intended restriction; the checks themselves are matching against an older form of that code.

The image-capability-ceiling self-test specifically failed two of five cases on its own terms: the committed ceiling value refuses a set of capability bits that current policy requires and admits one bit that no shipped capsule declares, which is a real mismatch between the committed ceiling and the current capsule catalogue, not a stale-text artifact.
Confirmed by an independent rerun: same failure, same error count.

Traced the CI configuration: the workflow that does run (`nix flake check`) does not include this script, and no release workflow depends on it; the workflow filename the script's own header names does not exist in the repository's CI directory.

Not tested: whether the equivalent GitHub-hosted CI run shows the same result (the checks involved are plain text and script checks with no external tool dependency, so a different result there was not expected but was not independently confirmed).

remediation: Update the stale text-pattern checks to match the current code, fix or re-derive the image-capability-ceiling values so the self-test passes, wire the script into a CI workflow that gates releases, and remove or correct the reference to the workflow file that no longer exists.
